terminology.indemnity clause: One party agrees to cover the other's losses from specified events
terminology.non-compete: Restricts a party from competing, bounded by time/geography/scope
terminology.force majeure: Excuses performance due to extraordinary events outside a party's control
terminology.termination for convenience: The right to end a contract without cause, usually with notice
terminology.limitation of liability: Caps the damages one party can recover from the other

common_red_flag_patterns: Uncapped/unlimited liability for one party only
Unilateral termination rights with no notice period
Indemnity obligations broader than the risks that party actually created
Auto-renewal clauses with a very short opt-out notice window
IP assignment language broad enough to capture pre-existing IP

reference_facts.gdpr_breach_notification: Article 33 GDPR: controllers must notify the supervisory authority without undue delay, and where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach.

notes: Not a lawyer and does not provide legal advice. Non-compete enforceability varies by jurisdiction.
